Suricata 7.0.10 logs tls.sni from the client side (client_connp.sni) and tls.ja4 from client_connp.ja4, and creates the JA4 state only while parsing a ClientHello: https://github.com/OISF/suricata/blob/suricata-7.0.10/src/output-json-tls.c (lines 149-151, 215-221) and https://github.com/OISF/suricata/blob/suricata-7.0.10/src/app-layer-ssl.c (lines 1544-1547, 997). Hence 'tls record has sni' => Suricata saw the client hello => JA4 present when enabled.

Suricata 7.0.10 JA4 string format: 10-char prefix (t/q, version 13/12/11/10/s3/00, d/i, 2-digit cipher count, 2-digit extension count, 2 ALPN chars) + '_' + 12 hex + '_' + 12 hex = 36 chars: https://github.com/OISF/suricata/blob/suricata-7.0.10/rust/src/ja4.rs (get_hash, version_to_ja4code).

JA4 is enabled by default when building Suricata 7.0.10 (configure option --disable-ja4, default enable_ja4=yes): https://github.com/OISF/suricata/blob/suricata-7.0.10/configure.ac line 2223. jasonish/suricata:7.0.10 reports 'JA4 support: yes' (suricata --build-info); digest sha256:f8e7d04babeaab8bfac7e327b09e8f7471f144b0b205bfc503f7dd3130a6d2e7.
Suricata license GPL-2.0: https://github.com/OISF/suricata/blob/suricata-7.0.10/LICENSE (GNU GPL Version 2, June 1991).

Community ID v1 = '1:' + base64 of a SHA-1 digest, default seed 0: https://github.com/corelight/community-id-spec (fetched). All 14 fixture eve.json files and the fresh ones: every record has a community_id matching ^1:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{27}=$ and present in Zeek's conn.log.

KAR-03 step 3 says the capture test checks report['tools'] for both tools. As the computed task asked, the Zeek part is in the per-capture test (tools['zeek'] is True) and 'both ran' is its own test, skipped with reason 'suricata is not installed here; the engine image has it' when shutil.which('suricata') is None. It also asserts the Suricata TLS event has a JA4 and the same community_id as Zeek's TLS event (this catches a Debian Suricata built without JA4 or a config regression; fixture-based unit tests cannot). A missing Suricata in CI is still caught by the workflow's 'suricata -V' step. Consider adding 'suricata --build-info | grep "JA4 support: *yes"' to that CI step.

must_not_contain contents (my choice; spec example lists 2): each cleartext capture lists the other 6 rules of the cleartext family (cleartext.* + rdp.standard_security); each TLS/cert capture lists the other 5 tls.*/cert.* rules. Reason: those read the same logs, so they are the plausible misfires; exactness over ALL rules is already checked on fixtures by tests/unit/test_rule_registry.py, and adding a new rule then does not require editing every expected file. Clean captures have only expected [] + expect_no_findings true (stricter, so no must_not_contain). Change to 'all 12 other rules' if you prefer.

Suricata eve test placed in tests/unit/test_suricata_eve.py: it only reads saved files (fast, runs in CI's unit job and on laptops). It honours FIXTURES_DIR (the same variable scripts/make_fixtures.sh uses), so fresh output can be checked: 'FIXTURES_DIR=/tmp/fresh bash scripts/make_fixtures.sh && FIXTURES_DIR=/tmp/fresh pytest tests/unit/test_suricata_eve.py -q'. It covers tests/fixtures/zeek/*/eve.json (14 lab captures), not _handmade/ (the Suricata 8 one has no conn.log). 'Client hello seen' is defined as 'tls record has sni' (sourced from Suricata 7.0.10 code); Zeek's TLS sessions are used as a second witness so the JA4 check cannot pass vacuously. Extra check beyond the brief: every eve community_id appears in Zeek's conn.log (seed 0 on both sides).

tests/integration/__init__.py and tests/integration/conftest.py were NOT created (not needed; unique test module basenames). Note for the docs: a second conftest.py in tests/integration would replace sys.modules['conftest'], so any future 'from conftest import ...' in tests would break; tests here compute paths from __file__ like the existing ones.

KAR-06 step 2 design choices to reflect in karthik.md: probes are fixed to port 80 (cleartext.http is port-based; 8080 would be http_alt) and port 23; both via curl (curl telnet://, so no telnet client needed), with --noproxy '*'; the service address must be an IPv4 number in RFC 1918 or RFC 5737 ranges (loopback, CGNAT, names, leading zeros, IPv6 refused, exit 2); exit 1 = probe/console failure or timeout; the console is checked once before probing (fail fast), later poll failures only warn; GET /api/alerts?limit=1000 (API maximum; newest first within a severity). Env: LIVE_CHECK_POLL_SECONDS (60), LIVE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1800). Needs bash, curl with telnet, python3 (JSON parsing; jq not assumed).

KAR-06 clock caveat: the script compares alert last_seen (sensor clock: when the traffic was seen) with the laptop's start time, so sensor and laptop clocks must agree (NTP). On an offline lab the Pi 5's clock may drift (its RTC needs a battery) - a hardware question for JAK-06/07. If that is a problem, the alternative is last_received_at (console clock), correct only when the script runs on the console machine.

doc_notes:
WHAT EACH FILE IS FOR
- tests/expected/<capture>.json (14): the answer key. Format (Fall 2026): capture, expected [{rule_id, dst_port, min_count}], must_not_contain [rule IDs], and for the two clean captures expect_no_findings: true. min_count is 1 because each lab capture has one session; counts are summed per (rule_id, dst_port) in case several findings share them.
- tests/integration/test_pcaps.py: parametrized over the expected files; runs maxguard.pipeline.analyze(capture, tmp_path, explain=False). Why integration tests at all: unit tests read saved logs, so only these notice when the way MaxGuard RUNS Zeek/Suricata breaks (proved: removing cleartext.zeek made telnet/pop3/imap fail; nothing else did).
- tests/integration/test_determinism.py: analyze twice into two DIFFERENT folders (so a leaked path also fails) and compare dicts. The small differences() helper turns a failure into exact paths, e.g. report['events'][0]['uid']: 'CVMEph...' != 'CeUBb0...' (seen when Zeek ran without -D). Its own unit test is unmarked on purpose so it runs in the fast job.
- tests/unit/test_suricata_eve.py: Community ID on every eve record (pattern ^1:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{27}=$: '1:' + base64 of 20-byte SHA-1), the same IDs in Zeek's conn.log, a JA4 on every TLS record with an SNI, and normalize() copying it (event_id == record_id('eve.json', rec)). SNI = proof Suricata parsed the client hello, because SNI only exists in the ClientHello and Suricata builds the JA4 while parsing that same message.
- scripts/live_check.sh: bash, set -euo pipefail, shellcheck-clean.
- docs-draft/test-results.md: the cross-check page (MaxGuard vs tshark), runs, failure demos, live_check results.

GOTCHAS
- Integration tests need Zeek; on a laptop run 'pytest -m "not integration" -q'. Missing Zeek is a FAILURE with a clear ZeekError message (never silently skipped), but missing Suricata is a visible SKIP, because the sandbox image lacks it; CI's 'suricata -V' step guards the real image.
- Inside the test image the tests run as user maxguard and /opt/maxguard is root-owned: tests must write only to tmp_path (they do).
- Running the stand-in: docker run --rm --network none --user $(id -u):$(id -g) -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 -e HOME=/tmp -v $PWD:/src -w /src maxguard-sandbox:test /opt/venv/bin/python -m pytest -m integration -q -p no:cacheprovider (sandbox only; never document the image name as a junior step).
- Suricata's flow_id is random per run (fresh eve.json differed from the fixtures ONLY there); record IDs ignore it, which is why determinism holds with Suricata too.
- tshark: TLS 1.3 encrypts the certificate, so clean_tls13 proves 'no rule fires on modern TLS', not 'its certificate is fine'. len(pkixalgs.modulus) < 257 means < 2048 bits because DER adds a leading zero byte to a full 2048-bit modulus. 'all x509af.utcTime < "2026-10-06"' compares both certificate dates with the capture day (like MaxGuard's rule: session time, never today). Self-signed needs awk because a display filter cannot compare two values of one field. Run tshark as --user 65534:65534 with --network none.
- live_check.sh: '--noproxy *' matters (a proxy in http_proxy would otherwise receive the probes: shown). Names are refused (a name can point anywhere); leading zeros refused (some tools read 010 as octal 8). The Telnet probe succeeds whenever the service sent something (MaxGuard only reports Telnet sessions where the server sent data), even if curl stops at its 10 s limit (exit 28) because a real service keeps asking for a password. 'last_seen >= start' (not count) is the right test because a repeat run updates the SAME alert (same finding_id): the second sandbox run proved count 1->2 and last_seen moved.
- Local test recipe used in planning (Linux): lab-server container on 'docker network create --internal <net>' (host can still reach the container's 172.x address), fake console 'python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory <dir>' serving <dir>/api/alerts (query string ignored), a background job rewriting that JSON atomically (write tmp + os.replace) with last_seen=time.time(); LIVE_CHECK_POLL_SECONDS=1 LIVE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=20. On Docker Desktop (macOS/Windows) container IPs are not reachable from the host: publish ports on the laptop's LAN address instead (not run).
